predecessors.name: Hungary, 1918-1946 (Cliopatria's 'Hungarian Republic' row)
predecessors.text: Hungary within the post-Trianon frontiers, to which the 1947 Paris treaty restored it ('reduced to its immediate post-Trianon borders'), less three villages near Bratislava

successors.name: Hungarian People's Republic
successors.text: the whole country within the frontiers of the 1947 Paris peace treaty, renamed the Hungarian People's Republic when the constitution was promulgated on 20 August 1949

ledger.x: 1946: the Second Hungarian Republic replaces the Kingdom.

1947: Hungary cedes three villages near Bratislava to Czechoslovakia under the Paris treaty ('three villages near Bratislava were also transferred to Czechoslovakia'; treaties signed 10 February 1947, effective 15 September 1947).
1949: the Second Republic ends and the Hungarian People's Republic follows.

certainty.note: Pre-1938 (Trianon) frontier restored in fact under Soviet occupation; the formal restoration followed with the treaty of 1947.
The frontier is the Trianon one as confirmed on 10 February 1947 (effective 15 September 1947) with the three villages near Bratislava ceded.
